BillHeading.Sponsors: Senators Nguyen, Wellman, Kuderer, Hasegawa, Lovelett, Salomon, Saldaña, and Hunt

BillHistory.ReferredCommittee: Referred to Committee on Ways & Means.

BillHeading.BriefDescription: Providing progressive tax reform by imposing an excise tax on annual compensation in excess of one million dollars.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to providing progressive tax reform by imposing an excise tax on annual compensation in excess of one million dollars; adding a new chapter to Title 50A RCW; and prescribing penalties.

BillSectionHeader.P: The definitions in this section apply throughout this chapter unless the context clearly requires otherwise.

BillSection.P: (1) "Commissioner" means the commissioner of the department defined in subsection (2) of this section.
(2) "Department" has the same meaning as in RCW 50A.04.010.

(3) "Employee" means an individual who is in the employment of an employer. The term "employee" includes individuals who are self-employed, sole proprietors, members of a limited liability company, partners of a partnership, governors as defined in RCW 23.95.105, and any other employer.
(4) "Employer" has the same meaning as in RCW 50A.04.010. For purposes of this chapter, an individual can be both an employer and an employee.

(5) "Employment" means personal service, of whatever nature, as known to the common law or any other legal relationship performed for wages or under any contract calling for the performance of personal services, written or oral, express or implied. The term "employment" includes an individual's entire service performed within or without or both within and without this state, if:
(a) The service is localized in this state; or
(b) The service is not localized in any state, but some of the service is performed in this state; and
(i) The base of operations of the employee is in this state, or if there is no base of operations, then the place from which such service is directed or controlled is in this state; or

(ii) The base of operations or place from which such service is directed or controlled is not in any state in which some part of the service is performed, but the individual's residence is in this state.
(6) "Service is localized in this state" has the same meaning as provided in RCW 50.04.120.
(7) "Wage" or "wages" has the same meaning as provided in RCW 50A.04.010.

BillSectionHeader.P: (1) Beginning January 1, 2020, the department must assess for each employee in employment of an employer an excess compensation tax on the employer based on the amount of an employee's wages at the rates established in subsection (2) of this section. Each employer must remit the tax to the department in a manner specified by the department.

BillSection.P: (2)(a)(i) Tier I. Wages received by an employee from an employer during a calendar year that exceed $999,999.99 but that do not exceed $4,999,999.99 must be taxed at a rate of five percent.

(ii) Tier II. Wages received by an employee from an employer during a calendar year that exceed $4,999,999.99 but that do not exceed $9,999,999.99 must be taxed at a rate of seven and one-half percent.
(iii) Tier III. Wages received by an employee from an employer during a calendar year that exceed $9,999,999.99 must be taxed at a rate of ten percent.
(b) In the payment of any taxes, a fractional part of a cent is disregarded unless it amounts to one-half cent or more, in which case it is increased to one cent.

BillSectionHeader.P: Employer requirements for this chapter are the same as the requirements in RCW 50A.04.080 (1) through (3).
(1) Employers are subject to the penalties in RCW 50A.04.090 (1), (4), and (5).

BillSection.P: (2) An employer who willfully fails to remit the full amount of the tax when due is liable, in addition to the full amount of the tax due and amounts assessed interest under section 6 of this act to a penalty equal to the tax and interest.
(3) Any moneys under this section must be deposited into the general fund of the state.

BillSectionHeader.P: To the extent not inconsistent with the provisions of this chapter, the following statutes govern the administration of the excess compensation tax act: RCW 50A.04.080, 50A.04.090, 50A.04.125, 50A.04.130, 50A.04.135, 50A.04.145, 50A.04.155 through 50A.04.185, 50A.04.265, 50A.04.500, 50A.04.505, 50A.04.515, 50A.04.520, 50A.04.530 through 50A.04.580, and 50A.04.595.

If taxes are not paid on the date on which they are due and payable as prescribed by the commissioner, the whole or part thereof remaining unpaid must bear interest at the rate of one percent per month or fraction thereof from and after such date until payment plus accrued interest is received by the commissioner. The date as of which payment of taxes, if mailed, is deemed to have been received may be determined by such rules as the commissioner may prescribe. Interest collected pursuant to this section must be paid into the general fund of the state. Interest may not accrue on taxes from any estate in the hands of a receiver, executor, administrator, trustee in bankruptcy, common law assignee, or other liquidating officer subsequent to the date when such receiver, executor, administrator, trustee in bankruptcy, common law assignee, or other liquidating officer qualifies as such, but taxes accruing with respect to employment of persons by any receiver, executor, administrator, trustee in bankruptcy, common law assignee, or other liquidating officer become due and draw interest in the same manner as taxes due from other employers. Where adequate information has been furnished to the department and the department has failed to act or has advised the employer of no liability or inability to decide the issue, interest may be waived.

BillSectionHeader.SectionCaption: COLLECTION BY DISTRAINT, SEIZURE, AND SALE—PROCEDURE.
BillSectionHeader.P: The commissioner, upon making a distraint, must seize the property and must make an inventory of the property distrained, a copy of which must be mailed to the owner of such property or personally delivered to him or her, and must specify the time and place when such property must be sold. A notice specifying the property to be sold and the time and place of sale must be posted in at least two public places in the county wherein the seizure has been made. The time of sale may be not less than ten nor more than twenty days from the date of posting of such notices. The sale may be adjourned from time to time at the discretion of the commissioner, but not for a time to exceed in all sixty days. The sale must be conducted by the commissioner or his or her authorized representative who proceeds to sell such property by parcel or by lot at a public auction, and who may set a minimum price to include the expenses of making a levy and of advertising the sale, and if the amount bid for such property at the sale is not equal to the minimum price so fixed, the commissioner or his or her representative may declare such property to be purchased by the department for such minimum price. In such event the delinquent account must be credited with the amount for which the property has been sold. Property acquired by the department as prescribed in this section may be sold by the commissioner or his or her representative at public or private sale, and the amount realized must be placed in the general fund of the state. In all cases of sale, as provided in this section, the commissioner must issue a bill of sale or a deed to the purchaser and such bill of sale or deed is prima facie evidence of the right of the commissioner to make such sale and conclusive evidence of the regularity of his or her proceeding in making the sale, and must transfer to the purchaser all right, title, and interest of the delinquent employer in said property. The proceeds of any such sale, except in those cases wherein the property has been acquired by the department, must be first applied by the commissioner in satisfaction of the delinquent account, and out of any sum received in excess of the amount of delinquent taxes, interest, and penalties the administration fund must be reimbursed for the costs of distraint and sale. Any excess that thereafter remains in the hands of the commissioner must be refunded to the delinquent employer. Sums so refundable to a delinquent employer may be subject to seizure or distraint in the hands of the commissioner by any other taxing authority of the state or its political subdivisions.

The commissioner may charge off as uncollectible and no longer an asset of the general fund of the state, any delinquent taxes, interest, penalties, or credits if the commissioner is satisfied that there are no cost-effective means of collecting the taxes, interest, penalties, credits, or benefit overpayments.
Moneys received by the state under this chapter must be deposited in the general fund of the state.
The department is exempt from the requirements of chapter 39.26 RCW until July 1, 2020, for purposes of implementing chapter 50A.--- RCW (the new chapter created in section 12 of this act).
This act may be known and cited as the excess compensation tax act.
Sections 1 through 11 of this act constitute a new chapter in Title 50A RCW.
